harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Configured, via an Ansible playbook run from control node node2, a root cron job on node1 that runs /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 and appends output to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log. Both managed nodes (node1, node2) were then restarted one at a time with verified boot-identity changes and confirmed post-restart recovery.
actions_performed: Identified node2 as the Ansible control node (ansible-core preinstalled, /root/.ansible.cfg configured for user antrieb + sudo become) and node1 (RHEL7) as the managed target
Established SSH trust node2->node1 by appending the cluster CLUSTER_SSH_PUBKEY to node1's antrieb authorized_keys (the preexisting key only covered the harbor exec bridge, not inter-node SSH)

Installed python3 then rh-python38 on node1 via yum/RHSCL; ansible-core 2.20 on node2 required target Python 3.9+ which RHEL7 cannot provide, so installed a separate ansible-core 2.16.14 in a venv on node2 (/root/ansible/venv216) which supports Python 3.8 targets

Wrote /root/ansible/inventory-maintenance-cron.yml on node2 using the ansible.builtin.cron module to add a root crontab entry: '15 2 * * * /usr/local/bin/inventory-maintenance >> /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log 2>&1'
Ran the playbook (changed=1), verified the root crontab entry on node1, and re-ran the playbook to confirm idempotency (changed=0)
Manually executed the exact cron command line on node1 to functionally verify it writes to /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
Captured baseline boot_id and health (crond active, crontab content, log content) on node1; baseline boot_id and control-tooling presence on node2
Restarted node1 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (0d6209e2... -> 46b864cf...), and verified crond active plus crontab and log file intact post-restart

Restarted node2 via systemctl reboot, polled until reachable, confirmed boot_id changed (416c5cf5... -> c1da0375...), and verified the ansible venv/ssh key were intact and the playbook still ran successfully (idempotent, changed=0) against node1 post-restart

evidence.requirement: Cron job scheduled via Ansible on node1 to run inventory-maintenance daily at 02:15 retaining output in /var/log/inventory-maintenance.log
evidence.summary: Playbook using ansible.builtin.cron applied to node1 from node2; crontab -l on node1 shows the exact 02:15 daily entry piping output to the log file.

evidence.requirement: Idempotency of the Ansible-managed cron job
evidence.summary: Second playbook run reports changed=0/ok=2, confirming the cron resource is stable/idempotent.

evidence.requirement: Functional verification that the scheduled command writes to the retained log
evidence.summary: Manually executed the exact cron command line on node1; log file was created/appended with the script's timestamped output.

evidence.requirement: SSH/Ansible connectivity setup from control node2 to node1
evidence.summary: Identified node2 as control node, wired cluster SSH keypair trust, and confirmed working ansible ping (pong) from node2 to node1 using ansible-core 2.16.14 venv compatible with node1's Python 3.8.

evidence.requirement: node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline captured (boot_id 0d6209e2..., crond active, crontab+log present); systemctl reboot acknowledged then connection dropped; polling showed timeout then success with new boot_id 46b864cf...; post-restart check shows crond active and crontab/log/script all intact.

evidence.requirement: node2 restart evidence: healthy baseline, restart, changed boot identity, recovered state
evidence.summary: Baseline captured (boot_id 416c5cf5..., ansible venv and ssh key present); systemctl reboot issued (stream closed on disconnect); polling showed timeout then success with new boot_id c1da0375...; post-restart check confirms ansible tooling intact and playbook run against node1 succeeds idempotently.
